answer: A registry that charges a refundable stake priced in quartz, a scarce verifiable resource, makes Sybil attacks expensive: each fake identity must lock real collateral that is slashed on fraud. Honest agents earn it back by doing useful work, like tending a shared meadow of verified services. The old fable of one wolf in many sheep's skins fails when every skin costs a deposit; an attacker wanting a thousand identities must pay a thousand deposits, and losing them all makes the attack unprofitable.
